description: LoCoMo-/LongMemEval-style public retrieval benchmark fixtures for Zavi memory. Each case is a self-contained multi-session conversation distilled into memory notes plus question/expected-note pairs. Hand-written in the public-dataset STYLE, NOT derived from any prod tenant — safe to commit and to ingest into a throwaway namespace. This is a SAMPLE harness (a few dozen questions), not the full published LongMemEval/LoCoMo run; the full datasets drop into this same { cases:[{notes,questions}] } shape for a published number. The set is deliberately HARD — paraphrased queries (query wording != note wording), per-conversation distractor notes (topically-similar but wrong), and multi-hop/temporal cases — so a lexical baseline scores BELOW 1.0 and the benchmark actually discriminates. Question types span LongMemEval's taxonomy: single-session fact recall, multi-session synthesis, temporal reasoning, knowledge-update (supersede / ordering), and abstention (off-topic negative).

cases.title: Two founders discussing their marketplace-analytics SaaS over several sessions

notes.title: Company and product
notes.body: Harbor is a B2B platform that gives online marketplaces live revenue and retention dashboards. It launched in 2023.

notes.title: Who leads what
notes.body: Devi serves as chief executive and leads investor relations and the sales motion. Tomas is the chief technology officer and owns the data ingestion pipeline.

notes.title: Plan pricing
notes.body: The Launch plan is billed at 99 dollars per month, the Scale plan at 499 dollars per month, and large accounts negotiate bespoke contracts.

notes.title: Planning cadence
notes.body: The leadership group holds a quarterly planning offsite to set the product roadmap and the hiring plan for the next two quarters.

notes.title: Dashboard capability
notes.body: Harbor's revenue dashboard renders cohort retention curves and live volume tracking for every marketplace seller account.

notes.title: Founder background
notes.body: Devi spent her childhood in Pune and competes in weekend bouldering events.

notes.title: Tech stack
notes.body: The services are written in Go, events are stored in ClickHouse, and the operator console is built with React and TypeScript.

notes.title: Growth milestone
notes.body: Harbor crossed 120 paying accounts during the second quarter of 2024, having started that year with only 40 accounts.

notes.title: First enterprise logo
notes.body: During the first quarter of 2024 Harbor closed its first enterprise logo, a regional logistics company.

questions.query: Who runs engineering and infrastructure, and what do they own?
How much does the Scale plan cost each month?
Can Harbor show cohort retention and live transaction volume for sellers?
How many paying accounts did Harbor have by Q2 2024?
Where did Devi grow up and what does she do on weekends?
What is a good recipe for sourdough bread?

cases.title: A user planning a trip across multiple sessions, then revising it

notes.title: Original destination
notes.body: The user planned a two-week trip to Japan in October, centered on Tokyo and Kyoto.

notes.title: Dietary need
notes.body: The user is vegetarian and asked for plant-based restaurant options.

notes.title: Budget
notes.body: The user fixed a total trip budget of 4000 dollars not counting airfare.

notes.title: Updated destination (supersede)
notes.body: The user revised everything: the October trip now heads to South Korea, built around Seoul and Busan.

notes.title: Travel companion
notes.body: The user is taking the trip with their sister, who is a professional photographer.

notes.title: Unrelated future idea
notes.body: The user also bookmarked a separate winter trip idea to Japan for skiing in Hokkaido.

questions.query: Any food restrictions for eating out?
Who is accompanying the user on the trip?
What budget did the user set excluding flights?
Where is the user's October trip going now after they changed their plans?

cases.title: An operator describing internal policies over time

notes.title: Refund window
notes.body: Refunds are granted within 14 days of purchase when the customer has consumed under 20 percent of their credits.

notes.title: Response SLA
notes.body: A first reply to any support ticket is due within 4 business hours, and full resolution is targeted at 2 business days.

notes.title: Escalation path
notes.body: Tier-1 agents route billing disputes to the finance desk and route outages to the on-call engineer.

notes.title: Data retention
notes.body: Raw event logs are kept for 90 days and then anonymized and rolled up into aggregates.

notes.title: Discount policy
notes.body: New annual customers receive a 20 percent discount for the first year.

notes.title: Credit grants
notes.body: Customers on the Scale plan get 5000 monthly credits included.

questions.query: How quickly must support give a first response to a ticket?
When can a customer receive a refund?
Who deals with payment disputes after tier-1 hands them off?
How long are raw event logs stored before anonymization?

cases.title: A coaching relationship with facts that update over time

notes.title: Fitness goal
notes.body: The member's goal is to run a half marathon in the spring.

notes.title: Injury history
notes.body: The member tore their left ACL in 2021 and recovered after surgery.

notes.title: Recent progress
notes.body: As of last month the member can comfortably run 10 kilometers without knee pain.

notes.title: Diet preference
notes.body: The member follows a high-protein diet and avoids dairy.

notes.title: Previous coach
notes.body: The member's previous coach focused on cycling sessions, not running.

notes.title: Old goal (superseded)
notes.body: Two years ago the member's goal was simply to walk 8000 steps a day.

questions.query: What event are they training for?
How far can the member run right now without pain?
Which knee was injured in the past?
What does the member eat and what do they avoid?

cases.title: A vendor agreement summarized clause by clause

notes.title: Term length
notes.body: The agreement runs for an initial term of 24 months with automatic renewal.

notes.title: Termination
notes.body: Either party may terminate for convenience with 60 days written notice.

notes.title: Payment terms
notes.body: Invoices are net 30 and late payments accrue 1.5 percent monthly interest.

notes.title: Notice address
notes.body: All formal notices must be delivered to the legal department at the registered office.

questions.query: How long is the initial contract term?
How much advance warning before ending the contract?
When are invoices due and what is the late fee?
